body.heading: It looks small, but it is not
paragraphs: The Moon looks like a small coin in the sky. That is because it is very, very far away. Things far away always look smaller than they are.
The Moon is really about 3,474 kilometres wide. That is like driving across a whole country. Four Moons side by side would nearly stretch across the Earth.

body.heading: Big or small next to Earth?
paragraphs: The Earth is much bigger than the Moon. If the Earth were a beach ball, the Moon would be about the size of a tennis ball next to it.
But the Moon is still huge compared to you. Astronauts who walked on it found mountains, wide flat plains, and craters made by crashing space rocks.

body.heading: Why it looks different sizes
paragraphs: Some nights the Moon looks bigger, especially when it is low near the rooftops. That is a trick your eyes and brain play on you.
High in the sky, the same Moon looks smaller. It has not changed at all. Your brain is just comparing it with different things.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: the Moon looks tiny in the sky, so how big is it really?
